title: Don Cossacks
capsule: The Don Cossacks (донцы) were a semi-autonomous community of predominantly Orthodox Slavic frontiersmen who settled along the lower Don River and coalesced into the Don Host (Voisko Donskoe) over the course of the sixteenth century. Practically independent of Muscovite authority, they raided the steppe and waged near-constant war against the Crimean Khanate and Ottoman fortresses while supplying Moscow with irregular cavalry; a band led by Ataman Yermak Timofeyevich began the conquest of the Siberian Khanate in 1582. In 1637 Don Cossacks stormed the strategic Ottoman fortress of Azov at the mouth of the Don, and their famous defence of the captured stronghold (the 1641 Siege of Azov) became a defining episode of Cossack lore, though Moscow ultimately declined to annex the prize.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Don Host's territorial extent is reasonably well documented from Russian imperial records, but precise boundaries of effective control vs. nominal suzerainty are uncertain, particularly on the steppe margins.
